items.title: Warning: Humans cannot reliably detect speech deepfakes

items.title: Cortical-striatal brain network distinguishes deepfake from real speaker identity

judge.evidence_topic: Here, we test the neurocognitive sensitivity of 25 participants to accept or reject person identities as recreated in audio deepfakes.
judge.evidence_empirical: Here, we test the neurocognitive sensitivity of 25 participants to accept or reject person identities as recreated in audio deepfakes.

items.title: Deepfake detection with and without content warnings

judge.evidence_topic: We conduct an experiment to measure people's alertness to and ability to detect a high-quality deepfake among a set of videos.
judge.evidence_empirical: We conduct an experiment to measure people's alertness to and ability to detect a high-quality deepfake among a set of videos.

items.title: Voice clones sound realistic but not (yet) hyperrealistic

judge.evidence_topic: We investigated the extent to which AI-generated voices sound real to human listeners, and whether listeners can accurately distinguish between human and AI-generated voices.
judge.evidence_empirical: We tested these questions using AI-generated voices generated with and without a specific human counterpart (i.e., voice clones, and voices generated from the latent space of a large voice model).
judge.reason: O artigo aborda a percepção humana de vozes sintéticas, enquadrando-se no tema. O estudo é empírico, utilizando testes com ouvintes humanos, e o método descrito é consistente com o resumo. O achado principal reflete com precisão as conclusões apresentadas no texto.

items.title: AI-synthesized faces are indistinguishable from real faces and more trustworthy

judge.evidence_topic: Our evaluation of the photorealism of AI-synthesized faces indicates that synthesis engines have passed through the uncanny valley and are capable of creating faces that are indistinguishable-and more trustworthy-than real faces.
judge.evidence_empirical: Our evaluation of the photorealism of AI-synthesized faces indicates that synthesis engines have passed through the uncanny valley and are capable of creating faces that are indistinguishable-and more trustworthy-than real faces.
judge.reason: O resumo confirma que o estudo avaliou o fotorrealismo de rostos sintéticos e concluiu que são indistinguíveis e mais confiáveis que rostos reais, o que sustenta o achado principal. A natureza empírica e o método de avaliação por humanos são inferidos corretamente a partir da descrição do fotorrealismo e da comparação com rostos reais.

items.title: What you see is not what you get anymore: a mixed-methods approach on human perception of AI-generated images

judge.evidence_topic: This study explores human perception and detection capabilities regarding AI-generated images of landscapes, architecture, and interiors using a mixed-methods approach.
judge.evidence_empirical: A total of 104 participants took part in an online survey, classifying 50 images (25 real, 25 AI-generated) from five leading TTI models.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (survey) sobre a percepção humana de imagens geradas por IA, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão e exclusão. Os dados extraídos estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Training human super-recognizers' detection and discrimination of AI-generated faces

judge.evidence_topic: Here, we investigate synthetic face detection and discrimination in super-recognizers (SRs; who have exceptional face recognition skills), and typical-ability control participants.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two different experimental designs, we found that SRs (total N = 283) were better at detecting and discriminating synthetic faces than controls (total N = 381)
judge.reason: O artigo é empírico e trata da detecção humana de rostos sintéticos, estando dentro do escopo. O método descrito (dois desenhos experimentais) condiz com o resumo. O achado principal é sustentado pelo texto. O dado de tamanho da amostra extraído pelo usuário continha texto extra, mas os valores numéricos estão corretos.

items.title: AI Images vs. Real Photographs: Investigating Visual Recognition and Perception

judge.evidence_topic: The study assessed how people perceive 12 pictures generated by AI vs. 12 real photographs.
judge.evidence_empirical: The visual perception of selected images was studied by means of eye tracking and gaze patterns as well as time characteristics
judge.reason: O artigo é empírico, trata da percepção humana de imagens sintéticas e o achado principal está presente no resumo. O tamanho da amostra não consta no resumo, conforme indicado nos dados extraídos.

items.title: People are poorly equipped to detect AI-powered voice clones

items.title: Perception and deception: Exploring individual responses to deepfakes across different modalities

judge.evidence_topic: This study is one of the first to investigate the relationship between modalities and individuals' tendencies to believe and share different forms of deepfakes (also deep fakes).

items.title: Real and Deepfake Face Recognition: An EEG Study on Cognitive and Emotive Implications

items.title: On the realness of people who do not exist: The social processing of artificial faces

judge.evidence_topic: Here, we focus on how people evaluate realistic-looking faces of non-existing people generated by generative adversarial networks (GANs).
judge.evidence_empirical: In three studies, we investigated if and how participants can distinguish between GAN and REAL faces and the social consequences of their exposure to artificial faces.

judge.evidence_topic: In Experiment 1 ( N = 124 adults), alongside our reanalysis of previously published data, we showed that White AI faces are judged as human more often than actual human faces—a phenomenon we term AI hyperrealism.

items.title: AI-generated images of familiar faces are indistinguishable from real photographs

judge.evidence_topic: Here, we investigated a new method for generating face images (via ChatGPT plus DALL·E) and its application to both fictional and real (in this case, celebrity) identities. Our results demonstrated that generated images of both fictional (Experiment 1) and celebrity identities (Experiment 2) could not be distinguished from real photographs.
judge.evidence_empirical: Here, we investigated a new method for generating face images (via ChatGPT plus DALL·E) and its application to both fictional and real (in this case, celebrity) identities. Our results demonstrated that generated images of both fictional (Experiment 1) and celebrity identities (Experiment 2) could not be distinguished from real photographs.
judge.reason: O artigo é empírico, trata da percepção humana de imagens sintéticas e os dados extraídos estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Training humans for synthetic face image detection

judge.evidence_topic: In this work, we address these challenges by designing an online experiment to evaluate human detection capabilities and the impact of training on detecting synthetic face images.

items.title: Testing human ability to detect 'deepfake' images of human faces

items.title: Too beautiful to be fake: Attractive faces are less likely to be judged as artificially generated

judge.evidence_topic: In this study, 150 participants rated 109 pictures of faces on 4 characteristics (attractiveness, beauty, trustworthiness, familiarity). The stimuli were then presented again with the new information that some of them were AI-generated, and participants had to rate each image according to whether they believed them to be real or fake.
judge.evidence_empirical: In this study, 150 participants rated 109 pictures of faces on 4 characteristics (attractiveness, beauty, trustworthiness, familiarity).
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico com participantes humanos que investiga a percepção de rostos sintéticos, atendendo aos critérios. O achado principal extraído está diretamente sustentado pela frase 'Our results suggest a gender-dependent role of attractiveness on reality judgements, with faces rated as more attractive being classified as more real' presente no resumo.

items.title: Perception and social evaluation of cloned and recorded voices: Effects of familiarity and self-relevance

judge.evidence_topic: In the present study, we investigated whether listeners' perception and social evaluation of state-of-the-art voice clones depend on whether the clone being heard is a replica of the self, a friend, or a total stranger.
judge.evidence_empirical: Forty-seven of these experimental participants (and 47 unfamiliar controls) rated the Trustworthiness, Attractiveness, Competence, and Dominance of cloned and recorded samples of their own voice and their friend's voice.
judge.reason: O achado extraído reflete precisamente o que está no resumo: 'We observed that while familiar listeners found clones to sound less (or similarly) trustworthy, attractive, and competent than recordings'.

items.title: Specific media literacy tips improve AI-generated visual misinformation discernment

judge.evidence_topic: Images generated using artificial intelligence (AI) have become increasingly realistic, sparking discussions and fears about an impending “infodemic” where we can no longer trust what we see on the internet. In this preregistered study, we examine whether providing specific media literacy tips about how to spot AI-generated images can reduce susceptibility to AI-generated visual misinformation (AIVM).
judge.evidence_empirical: In this preregistered study, we examine whether providing specific media literacy tips about how to spot AI-generated images can reduce susceptibility to AI-generated visual misinformation (AIVM). Participants were randomly assigned to one of three conditions, reading specific media literacy tips, general media literacy tips, or no media literacy tips (control).
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico com participantes humanos sobre a percepção de imagens geradas por IA, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão e exclusão. O método e o achado principal estão corretamente descritos e sustentados pelo resumo.
